BEEP:
Plays a SID beep.

BEEP [duration]

Duration is in milliseconds. The
default value when omitted is 200 ms.
CHKDSK:
Checks a disk and returns a status
report.

CHKDSK [drive:] [/V | /C]

  /V  Checks and fixes all formatted
      1581 subpartitions and all CMD
      DOS partitions, including native
      subdirectories.
  /C  Compacts the cartridge file system
      journal.

CMD /V reports validation completion;
its allocation report is not disk-wide.
Omit drive to check the current disk.
COPY:
Copies a file to another location, or
combines files on the same disk.

COPY source [destination] [/P]
COPY source1+source2[+...] destination

  source       File(s) to copy.
  destination  Target drive/file name.
               Defaults to the current
               drive and directory.
  /P           Suppresses confirmation
               prompt to overwrite an
               existing file.
DEL:
Deletes one or more files.

DEL [drive:]filename [/P]
DELETE [drive:]filename [/P]
ERASE [drive:]filename [/P]

Wildcards: * and ?.

  /P  Suppresses confirmation prompt.
DIR:
Displays a list of files on a disk.

DIR [path][pattern] [/B /L /O /S /W]

  [drive:][pattern]
  /B          Uses bare format (names
              only).
  /L          Uses lower-case.
  /O          List files in sorted order
  sortorder    N  By name (alphabetic)
               T  By type (alphabetic)
               S  By size (smallest
                  first)
               -  Prefix to reverse
               F  Append to preserve the
                  first directory entry
  /T          Lists files of given type
  type         D  DEL    P  PRG
               R  REL    S  SEQ
               U  USR
  /S          Displays files in all sub-
              directories (paths and
              file names only).
  /W          Uses wide list format.
DISKCOPY:
Copies the contents of one disk to
another.

DISKCOPY source: destination:
  source:       Drive to copy from.
  destination:  Drive to copy to.

Note: source and destination drive must
have matching 1541/1571/1581 formats.
On CMD devices, copies the selected
emulation partition only.
ECHO:
Displays messages, or turns command-
echoing on or off.

  ECHO [ON | OFF]
  ECHO [message]

Type ECHO without parameters to display
the current echo setting. ECHO. (no
space) will insert a blank line.
EDIT:
Edits one screen of text.

EDIT [filename]

Supported edit keys are cursor keys,
INST/DEL, CLR/HOME, and RETURN. RUN/STOP
exits and prompts to save.

Omit filename to be prompted at save.
To create a batch file, include a .BAT
extension.
BASIC:
Starts the C64 BASIC environment.

In BASIC, type SHELL to return.
FORMAT:
Formats a disk.

FORMAT drive: [/V:label] [/ID:id]
              [/F:format]

  /V:label   Specifies the volume label.
  /ID:id     Specifies the disk ID.
  /F:format  Specifies a CMD-FD format
             type: 81, DD8, HD8, ED8,
             DDN, HDN, EDN, S8 or SW.
HELP:
Displays help on MCS-DOS commands.

  HELP [command]

[command]
  Displays help on that command.

COMMAND /? also displays help. If no
command is specified, a list of valid
commands is displayed.
LABEL:
Creates, changes, or deletes the volume
label of a disk.

LABEL [drive:] [label]
MEM:
Displays the amount of used and free
memory in your system.

MEM
MOVE:
Moves a file to another location, or
renames a directory within its parent.

MOVE source destination [/P]

  /P  Suppresses confirmation prompt to
      overwrite an existing file.
PAUSE:
Suspends processing of a batch program
and waits for a key to resume.

PAUSE [message]
PRINT:
Sends the contents of a file to a
printer.

PRINT filename [4:|5:|LPT1|LPT2]

LPT1 and LPT2 are aliases of devices
4 and 5.
REM:
Records comments in a batch file.

REM [comment]
REN:
Changes the name of a file or directory.

REN [drive:]filename1 [drive:]filename2
RENAME [drive:]filename1
       [drive:]filename2

CMD native directory renaming updates
both its entry and its own header.
RUN:
Executes a program.

RUN [drive:]filename [/A address]

  /A  Load and jump at the decimal
      address.
TYPE:
Displays the contents of a file.

TYPE filename [/H[:n] | /T[:n] | /HEX]

  /H:n  Shows first n lines of file.
  /T:n  Shows last n lines of file.
  /HEX  Shows a hex view.
  /C    Specifies a number of bytes
        instead of lines.

n defaults to 10 lines or bytes if not
specified.
VOL:
Displays the volume label (disk name)
and disk ID, if they exist.
VER:
Displays the MCS-DOS version and
copyright information.

VER
VERSION
DISKID:
Changes the drive's two-character ID.

DISKID [drive:] [id]

ID must be two letters or digits. Omit
the ID to be prompted.
SET:
Displays, sets, or removes  environment
variables.

SET [variable=[string]]
SET /ENV
  variable  Specifies the environment
            variable name.
  string    Specifies a series of
            characters to assign to the
            variable.
  /ENV      Displays environment usage
            statistics.

Type SET without parameters to display
the current environment variables.

Variable names can be up to 8 characters
long, and values up to 32 characters.
ATTRIB:
Displays or changes file attributes

ATTRIB [+L | -L] [[drive:]filename]

  +   Sets an attribute.
  -   Clears an attribute.
  L   File lock attribute.
SYSINFO:
Provides technical information about
your computer.

SYSINFO
FIND:
Searches for a text string in a file.

FIND [/V] [/C] [/N] [/I] "string"
     [[drive:]filename]

 /V  Displays all lines NOT containing
     the specified string.
 /C  Displays only the count of lines
     containing the string.
 /N  Displays line numbers with the
     displayed lines
 /I  Ignores the case of characters
     when searching for the string
 "string"
     Specifies the text string to find.
 [drive:]filename
     Specifies a file to search.
DISKINIT:
Resets disk drive state and forces a
reread of the directory.

DISKINIT [drive:]

CMD drives are not supported.
TAPECOPY:
Loads and transfers one or more files
from tape to disk.

TAPECOPY [filename] [drive:]

  filename  The name of the file to seek
            and load.
  drive:    The drive to copy to.

If no drive is specified, the current
one is used. Omitting the filename will
seek to the first file and prompt for
saving.
KEY:
Binds command text to function keys.

KEY [/Fn:[command] ...] [/CLEAR:[n]]

  /Fn:command
    Binds a command to a function key.
    n is 1 to 7.
  /Fn
    Displays the current binding for
    the specified function key.
  /CLEAR:n
    Clears the binding for one function
    key.
  /CLEAR
    Clears all bindings.

Type KEY without parameters to display
all current bindings.
CD:
Changes or displays the current
directory or partition.

CD [drive:][path] [/D]
CHDIR [drive:][path] [/D]

  /D  Changes drive in addition to
      changing directory on that drive.
MD:
Creates a directory or partition.

MD [drive:][path] [/SIZE:n]
MKDIR [drive:][path] [/SIZE:n]

  /SIZE:n  Specifies the partition size
           for 1581 drives (minimum 120
           sectors, multiple of 40).
RD:
Removes a directory or partition.

RD [drive:][path] [/S [/P]]
RMDIR [drive:][path]

  /S  Removes all directories and files
      in the specified directory as
      well. Not supported on CMD native
      directories.
  /P  Suppresses confirmation prompt
      with /S.

CMD native directories must be empty.
CMD top-level partitions cannot be
removed with this command.
